messages.subject: Milweed
messages.text: Which of the 11 variety of milkweed you offer are best for north idaho zone4 with dry silt soil for late spring through fall. Do not want something aggressive or invasive

messages.subject: Re: Milweed
messages.text:
Hello Tom,
 

 If you're looking for non-invasive milkweeds for Zone 4 in northern Idaho, the best choice is the tuberous milkweed (Asclepias tuberosa). It grows in clumps, is hardy in zones 3 through 9, emerges late in the spring, blooms from late spring through summer, prefers full sun and well-drained soil, and is drought-tolerant once established.
 

 However, the showy milkweed (Asclepias speciosa) could also be a good choice if adaptability to the local environment is the top priority. It is common and widespread in Idaho, tolerates moderately dry sites and alkaline soils, and flowers in Idaho from late May to mid-August.
 

 We remain at your disposal should you have any further questions.
 

 Warmly,
